cls: Ketoanalogues of essential amino acids (nitrogen-free amino acid precursors)
pharm: Provide essential amino acids without nitrogen load; support low-protein diets in chronic kidney disease
quick: 1 tablet per 5 kg body weight/day (commonly ~4-8 tablets TID)
Use only if clearly needed; ensure adequate nutrition
Designed for CKD; requires concurrent low-protein diet
summary: Alpha ketoanalogues (ketoacid/keto-amino acid preparations, e.g., the combination marketed as Ketosteril) provide the carbon skeletons (keto- and hydroxy-analogues) of essential amino acids plus selected essential amino acids, without contributing nitrogen. Used together with a very-low-protein or low-protein diet, they allow utilization of urea nitrogen for amino acid synthesis, helping reduce nitrogenous waste accumulation and slow progression in chronic kidney disease while maintaining nutrition. Note: this is a nutritional/metabolic preparation and is not an FDA-approved drug; dosing follows manufacturer SmPC/clinical nephrology practice.
indications: Prevention and treatment of damage due to faulty/deficient protein metabolism in chronic kidney disease, combined with a low-protein diet (typically eGFR <25-45 mL/min)
Adjunct to a very-low-protein or low-protein diet to maintain nutrition and reduce uremic toxin generation

dosage.d: 1 tablet per 5 kg body weight per day
dosage.t: Divided with meals (e.g., 4-8 tablets three times daily)
dosage.n: Typical adult ~70 kg: about 14 tablets/day, divided

dosage.d: With low-protein diet ~0.6 g/kg/day (or very-low ~0.3-0.4 g/kg/day)
dosage.n: Dietary protein restriction is essential to efficacy

dosage.d: Adjust per body weight and nutritional/biochemical status

admin: Swallow tablets whole during meals to facilitate proper absorption and metabolism
Must be combined with an appropriate restricted-protein diet to be effective
Ensure adequate caloric intake to prevent catabolism
Monitor serum calcium given calcium-containing salts
moa: Supplies nitrogen-free keto-/hydroxy-acid analogues of essential amino acids that are transaminated in the body, incorporating waste urea nitrogen into new amino acids and protein. This reduces production and accumulation of nitrogenous metabolic waste (urea) while supplying essential amino acids, supporting protein nutrition on a restricted-protein diet.

relative: Hereditary phenylketonuria (some products contain phenylalanine analogues - check formulation)

preg: Limited specific data; ensure adequate nutrition in CKD. Use only if clearly needed under specialist supervision.
lact: Limited data on use during breastfeeding; use with caution and adequate nutritional oversight.
renal: Specifically intended for chronic kidney disease as an adjunct to dietary protein restriction; requires concurrent low-protein diet. Monitor renal function and electrolytes.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment described; limited data. Use with general caution.

moderate: Calcium-containing/calcium-affecting agents (e.g., vitamin D, calcium salts) - additive hypercalcemia risk (preparations contain calcium)
Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, bisphosphonates, iron salts - calcium can chelate/reduce absorption; separate dosing
minor: Aluminum-containing drugs - monitor with renal impairment
interactions.food: Take with meals; combine with prescribed low-protein diet
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum calcium; helps lower serum urea/BUN when used with protein restriction

serious: Hypercalcemia (with prolonged/high intake, especially with vitamin D)

monitoring: Serum calcium (periodically; reduce vitamin D if elevated)
counsel: These tablets work only together with the prescribed low-protein diet - follow the diet and adequate calorie intake
Keep all blood-test appointments to monitor calcium and kidney function
Separate from antibiotics like tetracyclines/quinolones, iron, and bisphosphonates by a few hours
Report symptoms of high calcium (nausea, constipation, confusion, excessive thirst)
pk: Metabolic effect over days-weeks with dietary adherence
Amino acids absorbed within hours of intake
Not characterized as a single agent (mixture of amino acid analogues)
Requires ongoing daily intake with diet
Store at room temperature, protect from moisture
pearls: Not an FDA-approved drug - a metabolic/nutritional preparation (e.g., Ketosteril); dosing per manufacturer SmPC and nephrology practice, not an FDA label
Effective only when paired with a controlled low- or very-low-protein diet - the diet is integral to therapy
Provides essential amino acids without a nitrogen load, reducing urea generation in CKD
Contains calcium salts - monitor for hypercalcemia, especially with concurrent vitamin D
Used to delay dialysis and manage uremic symptoms in selected CKD patients under specialist supervision
missed: If a dose with a meal is missed, take it with the next meal; do not double up. Maintain the prescribed daily total over the day.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely to cause acute toxicity; excessive intake (especially with vitamin D) may cause hypercalcemia. Management: stop the product, reduce calcium/vitamin D intake, supportive care, treat hypercalcemia if symptomatic.
